task_instance: Run `trl sft` (TRL's supervised fine-tuning CLI) end-to-end on a tiny local GPT2-architecture model and a tiny local text dataset, entirely offline, and verify the fine-tuned model is saved and reloadable.
evidence: Installed trl via `pip install trl` (v1.14.0, CLI at /usr/local/bin/trl). Since huggingface.co was blocked by the sandbox's egress proxy (403 Forbidden on hf_hub_download when trying to fetch the gpt2 tokenizer), built everything locally instead: (1) trained a ByteLevelBPETokenizer from a small local corpus (corpus.txt) and saved it plus a randomly-initialized 2-layer GPT2LMHeadModel (~42.7k params) to ./tiny_model; (2) built a 40-example local text dataset with `datasets.Dataset.from_dict` and exported it to ./tiny_dataset_parquet/train.parquet. Ran: `trl sft --model_name_or_path ./tiny_model --dataset_name ./tiny_dataset_parquet --learning_rate 1.0e-3 --num_train_epochs 1 --per_device_train_batch_size 4 --output_dir ./sft_output --report_to none --max_length 64 --logging_steps 1 --use_cpu` (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1). Training ran for 10 steps, loss decreased from 5.85 to 5.56, and printed '✅ Training completed. 💾 Model saved to ./sft_output.' Verified the deliverable by reloading the saved model/tokenizer from ./sft_output with AutoModelForCausalLM/AutoTokenizer and successfully generating tokens with model.generate(). Output directory contains config.json, model.safetensors, tokenizer files, training_args.bin, checkpoint-10/, and a README.md, confirming the SFT CLI produces a real, loadable fine-tuned model artifact. This demonstrates the skill's core deliverable (running `trl sft` to produce a fine-tuned model) works in this runtime; the only limitation encountered was that pulling models/datasets/tokenizers from the Hugging Face Hub is blocked by network policy, which was worked around by using fully local artifacts rather than being a blocker to the CLI itself.
